mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) over a 6-month horizon signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings growth and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines persistently but S&P 500 forward returns remain positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% over a 3-month period signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 6.5% but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over a 3-month period signals monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% and remains elevated for 3 months
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above 1,200 units over a 6-month period signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST rises above 1,200 units but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
